premises: Nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at grain boundaries reduces grain boundary cohesion in CrMnFeCoNi.
This nanoclustering promotes intergranular cracking and ductility loss at intermediate temperatures.
Pre-existing Cr-rich secondary phases can act as alternative sinks for segregating elements.
Engineering grain boundaries with such secondary phases suppresses harmful nanoclustering.
Suppressing nanoclustering retains grain boundary cohesion and improves toughness/ductility.
